unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Assume that
\[
\left\|\frac1{\sqrt T}\sum_{i=1}^TZ_{i,k}\right\|_2>c\text{ for }k=1,\ldots,p_1,
\]
(11)
where $c>0$ is a constant. If there exist two constants $\alpha_s$, $\alpha_l$ such that $0<\alpha_s<\alpha_l<1$ and
\[
\frac{2\alpha_{p_1}}m+2\alpha B<(\alpha-1)\alpha_s,\quad\frac{4\alpha_{p_1}}m+4\alpha B+\alpha_s<\alpha_l,\quad\frac{12\alpha_{p_1}}m+12\alpha B+\alpha_l<1
\]
and
\[
4\alpha B<(\alpha-1)\alpha_s,\quad8\alpha B+\alpha_s<\alpha_l,
\]
(12)
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Theorem1’s uniform nondegeneracy (11) and all five dimension/block-exponent inequalities (12). Retain the independent growth exponents B and alpha_p1, together with 0<alpha_s<alpha_l<1. These general-combination conditions are not imported through Theorem4’s reference to the numeric v_T definition.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Suppose further that $d=O(T^{\beta_X})$ is a positive integer and the sets $\mathcal H\subset\{0,1,\ldots,d\}$, $\mathcal I\subset\{1,2,\ldots,d\}$ are not empty. Assume that there exists constants $0<\alpha_s<\alpha_l<1$ such that
\[
\frac{2\beta_X}m+2\alpha_X\beta_X<(\alpha_X-1)\alpha_s,\quad\frac{4\beta_X}m+4\alpha_X\beta_X+\alpha_s<\alpha_l,\quad\frac{12\beta_X}m+12\alpha_X\beta_X+\alpha_l<1
\]
and
\[
4\alpha_X\beta_X<(\alpha_X-1)\alpha_s,\quad8\alpha_X\beta_X+\alpha_s<\alpha_l
\]
(17)
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Theorem2’s common nonempty lag sets, lag growth and five inequalities (17). Shared by its two branches and by Theorem4(i)–(ii), but not the fixed-order AR branches.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
If a constant $c>0$ exists such that
\[
\left\|\frac1{\sqrt T}\sum_{i=1}^T(X_iX_{i-j}-\sigma_j)\right\|_2>c\text{ for }j\in\mathcal H,
\]
(18)
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Autocovariance nondegeneracy (18), restricted to j in H. This premise belongs to Theorem2(i) and Theorem4(i), not their autocorrelation branches.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
suppose there exists a constant $c>0$ such that
\[
\left\|\frac1{\sqrt T}\sum_{i=1}^TZ_{i,j}\right\|_2>c\text{ for }j\in\mathcal I\text{ and }\sigma_0>c.
\]
(20)
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Autocorrelation nondegeneracy (20), including sigma_0>c, restricted to j in I. Use the Theorem2(ii) definition of Z, not Theorem1 or the AR Z.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Let $p$ be a positive integer such that $p=O(1)$. In addition suppose that $\{X_i\}$ is weakly stationary and there exists a constant $c>0$ such that the smallest eigenvalue of $\Sigma$ is greater than $c$. Define $Z_{i,j}$ as in (27) and assume
\[
\left\|\frac1{\sqrt T}\sum_{i=1}^TZ_{i,j}\right\|_2>C\text{ for a constant }C>0\text{ and any }j=1,\ldots,p.
\]
(28)
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Fixed positive integer order, explicit weak stationarity, uniform minimum eigenvalue bound and AR nondegeneracy (28). Theorem4(iii) inherits the assumptions of Theorem3 through Lemma4(iii).

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Suppose $K(\cdot):\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$ is a kernel function satisfying Definition 2 and $k_T\to\infty$ as $T\to\infty$. The random variables $\{X_i,i\in\mathbb Z\}$ are $(m,\alpha_X)$-short range dependent with $m\ge8$, $\alpha_X>2$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Common Lemma4 assumptions explicitly imported by Theorem4. The corresponding branch assumptions are archived separately in A7–A9.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: (i) Suppose that $d=O(T^{\beta_X})$ is a positive integer, that the set $\mathcal H\subset\{0,1,\ldots,d\}$ is not empty and that (17) and (18) hold true.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Lemma4(i) assumptions imported for Theorem4(i). The covariance-estimator conclusion of Lemma4 is not an extra hypothesis or the definition of the bootstrap statistic.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: (ii) Suppose that $d=O(T^{\beta_X})$ is a positive integer, the set $\mathcal I\subset\{1,\ldots,d\}$ is not empty and that (17) and (20) hold true.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Lemma4(ii) assumptions imported for Theorem4(ii). Its estimated linearization is a covariance-estimation object, not the nonlinear bootstrap autocorrelation definition (40).

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: (iii) Suppose that the conditions of Theorem 3 are satisfied.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Lemma4(iii) explicitly imports the complete assumptions of Theorem3. Theorem4(iii) therefore inherits weak stationarity, fixed order, dependence and AR nondegeneracy; no analogous whole-Theorem1 import follows from defining v_T.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: (i) In addition suppose $d=O(T^{\beta_X})$ is a positive integer, the bandwidth $k_T$ is such that $v_T\times T^{7\alpha_X\beta_X}=o(1)$ and $k_T\times T^{8\beta_X/m+7\alpha_X\beta_X-1/2}=o(1)$, and the set $\mathcal H\subset\{0,1,\ldots,d\}$ is not empty. Suppose (17) and (18) hold true.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Theorem4(i) bandwidth conditions; its (ii) branch repeats the same rates. Preserve 7*alpha_X*beta_X and 8*beta_X/m+7*alpha_X*beta_X−1/2. These are not the weaker covariance-estimator rates of Lemma4.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: (iii) In addition suppose $p=O(1)$ is a positive number and the bandwidth $k_T$ satisfies $v_T=o(1)$ and $k_T\times T^{-1/2}=o(1)$. Suppose (28) hold true and assume that the smallest eigenvalue of the covariance matrix $\Sigma$ (see Theorem 3) is greater than a constant $c>0$.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Theorem4(iii) fixed-order bandwidth conditions v_T=o(1), k_T*T^(−1/2)=o(1), with (28) and the minimum eigenvalue bound. Preserve the printed positive-number wording for p; the inherited context requires an integer.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
Recall the definition of a sample quantile: For a numerical sequence $a_b$, $b=1,\ldots,B$ such that $a_1\le a_2\le\cdots\le a_B$,
\[
C^*_{1-\alpha}=a_{b^*},\text{ where }b^*=\min\left\{b=1,\ldots,B:\frac1B\sum_{c=1}^B\mathbf1_{\{a_c\le a_b\}}\ge1-\alpha\right\}.
\]
(42)
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Finite-bootstrap empirical quantile with its exact tie convention. Theorem4 concerns the exact conditional law. The separate B→infinity simulation approximation is discussed in prose and is not a missing fourth theorem branch.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original:
the solution of the $p$th order system of Yule-Walker equation, determines the coefficients of the best linear predictor of $X_i$ in the Hilbert space spanned by $X_{i-1},\ldots,X_{i-p}$. More precisely, the best linear predictor of $X_i$ is given by $\sum_{j=1}^p\beta_jX_{i-j}$, which by (2.7.15) in Brockwell and Davis (1991), satisfies
\[
EX_iX_{i-k}=\sum_{j=1}^p\beta_jEX_{i-j}X_{i-k}\text{ for }k=1,2,\ldots,p
\]
(25)
and, therefore, coincides with (23).
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Interpretation of Definition3 as linear prediction for a general weakly stationary series. Do not add the fitted AR model (22) or iid innovations as generating assumptions.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Define the filter $\mathcal F_i$ as the $\sigma$-field generated by $\ldots,e_{i-2},e_{i-1},e_i$ and $\mathcal F_{i,k}$ as the $\sigma$-field generated by $e_{i-k},e_{i-k+1},\ldots,e_i$, where $i\in\mathbb Z$ and $k\ge0$. Using these definitions, $X_{i,j}$ is $\mathcal F_i$ measurable.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Filtration context for the causal construction. Conditional projections used in main-text lemmas or proofs are not added as theorem statement dependencies.

unranked_auxiliary_passages.statement_original: Observations $X_1,\ldots,X_T$, the maximum lag $d$, the lag for calculating AR coefficients $p$ ($p\le d$), the kernel function $K(\cdot):\mathbb R\to[0,\infty)$, a bandwidth $k_T$, the nominal coverage probability $1-\alpha$ and the number of bootstrap replicates $B$. We also need the index set $\mathcal H\subset\{0,1,\ldots,d\}$ for autocovariances and the index set $\mathcal I\subset\{1,2,\ldots,d\}$ for autocorrelations.
unranked_auxiliary_passages.scope_note: Algorithm1 input domains, including p≤d and the different lag-zero conventions for H and I. The nominal level and finite simulation count are implementation inputs; Theorem4 controls the exact conditional laws.

source_issues.note: Remark2 prints sum from l=k to infinity of delta_m(k), whereas Definition1 uses delta_m(l). Preserve both. The explicit beta=0 specialization identifies the intended short-range condition; the literal constant-summand display is inconsistent except in degenerate cases.

Theorem2(i) prints unbound j in both covariance factors instead of j1 and j2. The intended two-lag covariance is shown correctly in Lemma4(i), equation(30). No repair is inserted into the original theorem statement or the CDF definition that refers to it.

Equation(27) prints sigma_k^(i), without a definition of this time-indexed quantity in the main text. Weak stationarity suggests E X_i X_(i−k)=sigma_k. Preserve the printed superscript and record this inferred interpretation separately; do not pretend a source definition was found.

The causal construction allows independent nonidentically distributed innovations and functions that vary with i,j,T. Theorem1 need not be weakly stationary. Section3 assumes weak stationarity for autocovariance/autocorrelation inference, and Theorem3 explicitly assumes it; this is not strict stationarity. Parameters and Gaussian approximants may change with T.

Read Theorem4’s Lemma4 reference branchwise: common kernel/dependence assumptions plus the corresponding (i),(ii),(iii) premise. Importing all three branches simultaneously would spuriously require an AR model/order in pure autocovariance inference and impose growing-lag constraints on the fixed-order AR result.

Theorem4 says define v_T as in Lemma3. This imports the three-case numerical sequence and its parameter alpha=alpha_X, not Lemma3’s whole-Theorem1 assumption reference or its covariance estimator conclusion.

The source gives no explicit value for sample or bootstrap correlations if their lag-zero denominator vanishes. Population autocorrelation inference assumes sigma_0>c. The original sample Yule–Walker definition specifies solving a system; only the bootstrap definition explicitly uses a Moore–Penrose inverse. Domain conventions remain separate from source transcriptions.

Definition3 concerns general-process Yule–Walker coefficients, not a linear AR data-generating restriction. Theorem3 has positive integer p=O(1); Theorem4(iii) prints positive number but inherits that integer setting. A strictly positive spectral density is a sufficient condition in prose, not an extra theorem premise.

d first denotes vector dimension and later maximum lag; e_i is an innovation and later a coordinate vector; B is a growth exponent, an AR derivative matrix, and a bootstrap-replicate count. Alpha is a decay exponent or nominal error probability, depending on context. Z and xi are redefined between theorems; preserve paper-local scope.

Definition2 imposes K(0)=1, not integral K=1. Nonnegative integrable Fourier transform yields positive-semidefinite multiplier covariance. The Gaussian example is optional. Preserve the printed unusual word di-fferentiable without altering its mathematical meaning.

Theorem4 bounds conditional Gaussian-bootstrap CDF errors with outer stochastic rates. Only branch(i) gives the explicit sum of sixth-root Op rates; branches(ii),(iii) state op(1). Finite B simulation quantile error is separate, discussed using B→infinity in prose; T4 is not an exact finite-sample coverage theorem.

Observed lag-product sums start at j+1 and have denominator T. Gaussian covariance targets use ideal centered sums over i=1..T of the infinite process. No circular or zero-padded data, sample-mean subtraction, T−j denominator or stationary simplification is silently inserted into Theorem1.

Uniform positive lower bounds concern the standard deviation of each normalized centered sum, not merely the variance of X_i. The autocorrelation branch additionally requires sigma_0>c. Keep all five exponent inequalities in(12) and(17), but use(17) only for growing-lag covariance/correlation branches; AR order remains O(1).

T1.standing_context: Mean-zero causal triangular array via short-range Definition1/Remark2; no weak stationarity.
T1.parameters: m≥8, alpha>2; positive d=O(T^B); p1=O(T^alpha_p1); deterministic coefficient row-square bound; separate B and alpha_p1.
T1.conclusion: Kolmogorov approximation of the maximum of p1 normalized linear combinations by a mean-zero Gaussian vector with the displayed T-dependent covariance.

T2.standing_context: Section3 mean-zero weak stationarity, possibly T-dependent law.
T2.conclusion: Two Gaussian approximation statements in one Theorem environment; branch premises remain separate.

T3.standing_context: Explicit weak stationarity; general time series, not a linear AR data-generating model.
T3.conclusion: Gaussian maximum approximation for fixed-order Yule–Walker estimation error; unresolved sigma_k^(i) notation retained.

T4.standing_context: Common Lemma4 kernel and short-range hypotheses, plus corresponding branch assumptions; Section3 or T3 weak-stationarity context.

i.rate: Op sum of two sixth-root terms in (45)

ii.rate: op(1) in (46); A10 stores the identical bandwidth restrictions from branch(i)

T4.conclusion: Conditional bootstrap maximum-CDF approximation; B→infinity empirical-quantile context A12 is separate.

ambient_conventions: Real random variables, expectation, Gaussian vectors, finite sums, absolute values and real matrices are ambient mathematical objects; library availability is not assessed.

O,o concern deterministic asymptotic quantities; Op,op concern stochastic quantities, with T the observed sample size. All uniformity and dimension-growth restrictions are preserved in the theorem statements and auxiliary conditions.
There are no implication-only dependency edges. Inline numerical assumptions remain branch-specific source context rather than invented named definitions.
